title: Stop Using ChatGPT Wrong: The Prompting Trick Nobody Teaches
angle: Most people treat ChatGPT like a search engine. The real trick is treating it like a method actor — give it a role, a constraint, and a format, and it transforms completely.

scenes.scene_name: The Hook — You've Been Doing It Wrong
scenes.voiceover: If you're typing plain questions into ChatGPT, you're getting maybe 10% of what it can do.
scenes.visual_description: Bold red text slams onto black screen: '10%'. Camera shakes. Text shatters and reforms as '100%' in gold.

scenes.scene_name: The Problem — Generic In, Generic Out
scenes.voiceover: Ask it a plain question, you get a plain answer. Boring. Useless. Everyone's getting the same output.
scenes.visual_description: Screen shows a bland ChatGPT response to 'write me an email'. Red X stamps over it. Cut to another bland reply. Another X. Rapid-fire.

scenes.voiceover: Here's the trick: Role. Constraint. Format. Three words that unlock elite-level outputs every single time.
scenes.visual_description: Three words fly in one by one — ROLE (blue), CONSTRAINT (orange), FORMAT (green) — each hitting the screen with a punch sound. They stack and lock together like puzzle pieces.
scenes.caption_overlay: R.C.F — the only prompt framework you need 🔑

scenes.voiceover: Watch. Same task. Without RCF vs with RCF. The difference is embarrassing.
scenes.visual_description: Split screen. Left: plain prompt, mediocre output highlighted in red. Right: RCF prompt fires in, elite detailed output floods the screen highlighted in green. Zoom punch on the right side.

scenes.voiceover: Marketing copy, code reviews, job applications, business plans — RCF works on literally everything.
scenes.visual_description: Rapid-cut montage: glowing laptop screens, someone pumping fist at a response, calendar filling with wins, cash emoji graphics exploding. Each cut lands on a beat.

scenes.voiceover: Still typing plain questions? You're still at 10%. Use RCF. The gap between you and everyone else just became massive.
scenes.visual_description: '10%' reappears in red — then explodes into '100%' in gold, mirroring scene 1. Final frame: 'R.C.F.' burns into the screen. Hard cut to black.
scenes.caption_overlay: Don't go back to 10% 🔥 Save this.

hook_test.format_reference: Stop Scrolling if you X — direct call-out format
hook_test.viral_proof: Variants like 'Stop using Google — use THIS instead' and 'You're using [tool] wrong' have repeatedly cracked 10M–50M views on TikTok and Reels (e.g., @techwithtim, @ai_explained style videos). The shame-hook + immediate fix structure is a proven retention driver.
hook_test.why_it_works: It opens with an accusation the viewer secretly fears is true (they're doing it wrong), then immediately promises a fix. This creates a curiosity-shame loop that prevents scrolling — viewers must stay to resolve the tension.
